chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said:

It was said to Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa, Allah’s blessings be upon them: What is it with these Muslims that they hate death? He said: Because they have become ignorant of it, so they hate it. If they were to know it and they were among the Allies of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, they would surely have loved it, and they would surely have known that the Hereafter is better for them than this world. Then he, peace be upon him, said: O father of Abdullah, what is it with a child or an insane person that he refrains from the medicine that cleans his body and negates the pain from him? He said: Due to their ignorance of the benefit of the medicine. He said: By He who sent Muhammad with the Truth as a Prophet, indeed, the one who prepares for death a true preparation, it is more beneficial to him than this medicine (that is given) to he who is treated. Verily, if they, indeed, were to know what death leads to of bliss, they would surely have called for it and loved it by the most intense of what a rational calls for medicine in order to repel misfortunes and draw safeties.
ai.seo_question: Why do Muslims hate death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates that the aversion to death stems from a lack of gnosis (*ma'ifa*) regarding the transition to eternal bliss, rather than death itself being undesirable. He employs the analogy of a child rejecting purgative medicine to illustrate how ignorance blinds believers to the spiritual cure death provides, whereas true *awliya* (friends of God) eagerly anticipate it as the ultimate purification and entry into a realm superior to worldly life.
